chunks: Masʿadah ibn Ṣadaqah narrated that a speaker said:

To Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام: “May I be your ransom, I pass by a group of Nāṣibīs, and the salat has been established for them while I am not in a state of wudu (ablution). If I do not enter with them in the salat, they will say whatever they wish to say. Should I pray with them, then perform wudu when I leave, and pray?”
Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام said: “Glory be to Allah! Does one who prays without wudu not fear that the earth may seize him in collapse?”

key_terms.خَسْفًا: swallowing or collapse of the earth, expressing severe divine punishment
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ: an expression of glorifying Allah, used here to show strong rejection
key_terms.نَاصِبِيَّةٍ: people hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.وُضُوءٍ: wudu (ablution), the required state of ritual purity for salat

ai.seo_question: Can someone join congregational prayer without wudu out of fear of what people will say?
ai.summary: This hadith rejects performing salat without wudu (ablution), even under social pressure from hostile people. Imam Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام strongly condemns such an act, emphasizing the gravity of intentionally praying in a state of ritual impurity.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1127 - Mas’adah ibn Sadaqah narrates that someone said to Jafar ibn Muhammad (as):

"May I be your ransom! I pass by a group of Nasibis (those hostile to the AhlulBayt (as)), and their prayer has been established while I am not in a state of wudu (ritual purity). If I do not join them in prayer, they will say whatever they wish about me. Should I then pray with them and perform wudu afterward and pray again?"
Jafar ibn Muhammad (as) responded: "Glory be to Allah (swt)! Does he not fear that if he prays without wudu, the earth would swallow him up?"
